question.text: The upfront payment made by an option buyer to the option writer is called the:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XII pages 201 and 208-209, the upfront payment made by an option buyer to the option writer is called the option premium. It is the price paid to acquire the right embedded in the option. The Trap: Strike price is the price at which the underlying can be bought or sold, not the upfront payment. Margin money is collateral deposited with the clearing corporation (relevant for futures and option writers). Settlement amount is the payout determined at expiry. Note: The option premium is the source-defined term for the upfront amount the buyer pays the writer.
